note: The World Inequality Database (WID.world, bulk download of 15 October 2026, read again in that of 30 October 2026), Russia, 2024: average net personal wealth (ahweal992j) and average post-tax national income (adiinc992j) per adult over 20, resources split equally within couples, in RUB of that year, for the bottom 20, 40, 60, 90 and 99 percent and the top 1 percent; each family's band is read from them. Read 2026-10-30. Read again 2026-11-03 from the bulk download of 30 October 2026 (its country files dated 30 October 2026): every row quoted here, its year and its currency label stood as before, and no later year was given. Until 2026-11-03 this note and its sources wrote the variable codes with their age and population parts swapped (ahwealj992 for ahweal992j and adiincj992 for adiinc992j), codes no file of the database holds (its README: type, concept, age group, population, as in sptinc992j), and called adiinc992j post-tax disposable income, which its metadata names post-tax national income ([Post-tax national income]=[Post-tax disposable income]+[Public spending]). The national accounts (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-03: each band's income scaled by households' disposable income over national income), read 2026-11-03: the latest households' account published for this country was in UNdata's National Accounts Official Country Data (the United Nations Statistics Division's), Table 4.6 and Table 4.1, series 1000, SNA 2008, for 2013: the net disposable income (B.6n) of households (S.14), 41,477,700,000,000 less 1,928,110,000,000 (39,549,590,000,000), over net national income (B.5n) 70,439,200,000,000 less 7,931,720,000,000 (62,507,480,000,000), in the table's currency (Russian Ruble), about 0.633. A ratio stands only from 2019 on (the lead's ruling of 2026-11-03), so it wasn't held, and each band's income stayed the database's post-tax national income, public spending included. The national accounts (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-03: each band's income scaled by households' disposable income over national income), searched again on 2026-11-03 in the statistics office's own accounts for a households' disposable income account from 2019 on, found none: Rosstat (rosstat.gov.ru, gks.ru, showdata.gks.ru), 2026-11-03: the TLS chain is not trusted here (self-signed certificate in chain) or the connection is reset; verification was not turned off. fedstat.ru answers 403. Common Crawl: rosstat.gov.ru/statistics/accounts captured 2024-08-12 (CC-MAIN-2024-33) lists only GDP, GVA, GRP, consolidated accounts (Consolidated_accounts_1995-2023.xlsx, economy-wide), input-output and supply-use tables, financial accounts and the balance of assets; no household sector account. That consolidated workbook and the mediabank files are not in CC-MAIN-2024-46, 2024-51, 2025-08 or 2025-13; from 2025 every rosstat.gov.ru capture is a 302 to ssl.rosstat.gov.ru. The yearbook "Национальные счета России в 2017-2024 гг." (rosstat.gov.ru/folder/210/document/13221), which carries the sector accounts, is only captured as a 302 (CC-MAIN-2025-18); the Wayback Machine refused the connection (429, then reset). Common Crawl: the Russian Statistical Yearbook 2023 index (rosstat.gov.ru/storage/mediabank/Ejegod_2023.htm, CC-MAIN-2024-46) lists section 12 "Система национальных счетов" as storage/2024/03-26/WoEtFaIx/Ejegod_2023/Ejegod_12-2023.xlsx; that file is in none of CC-MAIN-2024-38, 2024-42, 2024-46, 2024-51, 2025-05, 2025-08. Web search (Russian) for the households secondary-distribution account, 2026-11-03: regional disposable-resources survey releases only. The 2013 UNdata ratio was the newest found. Each band's income stayed the database's post-tax national income, public spending included.
